A1.justification: Both are complete, readable 24-page versions of LightMem. Text extraction and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E despite text reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo experiments in Tables 2–3, with ablations and supplementary analyses in Figure 3 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and analyses and adds GLM-4.6 results on LongMemEval-S in Table 2.

M1.justification: The compression, hybrid topic segmentation, STM summarization, timestamp-constrained soft updates, and offline parallel updates remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendix C. GLM-4.6 is an additional evaluation backbone, without a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo with the same conversational-memory tasks and question categories. The GLM-4.6 addition changes model configuration, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained GPT/Qwen experiments is unchanged, including both MemoryOS variants on LoCoMo. The new GLM-4.6 block reuses Full Text, Naive RAG, LangMem, and A-MEM; it introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Table 2 add GLM-4.6 evaluation on LongMemEval-S with three reported compression-ratio/STM-threshold configurations. Existing GPT/Qwen settings, data handling, metrics, and judging procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Compression and STM-threshold sensitivity analyses, segmentation comparisons and ablations, the soft-update case study, and category-wise analyses are unchanged in Sections 5.3–5.6 and Appendix C. The added GLM block contains ordinary benchmark results.

E5.justification: Results remain point estimates without reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional GLM rows introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds GLM-4.6 results: LightMem achieves 72.80–73.20% accuracy, versus 70.60% for A-MEM and 73.20% for Naive RAG, with reported token totals of 30.46–30.61k. No GLM offline-update outcomes are reported. Matched GPT/Qwen results, LoCoMo results, and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Section 3, complexity derivation in Section 4, and notation in Appendix A.2 are unchanged. Removing the descriptive human-memory background does not remove mathematical theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the three-stage memory contribution and the same performance-efficiency claims for GPT/Qwen. The GLM results do not introduce a new central claim or redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations of compression/buffer trade-offs, segmentation benefits, and soft-update information preservation remain unchanged, as do privacy/bias qualifications and future-work boundaries. The deleted human-memory overview is background exposition; no new interpretation of the GLM findings is supplied.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a future code-release promise with a project link and a statement that code is available. Implementation details, hardware, and prompts are unchanged. Table 5 still lists only GPT/Qwen, and the reproducibility statement still promises a future release.

R1.justification: v4 removes the human-memory background subsection and the references to Atkinson and Shiffrin (1968) and Rasch and Born (2013). The abstract and conclusion still invoke Atkinson–Shiffrin inspiration; Section 6 and positioning against computational prior work remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction is shortened, v2 Section 2.2 is removed, the remaining preliminary subsection is renumbered, and acknowledgments are added. Headers change from work-in-progress wording to ICLR 2026 publication wording. Most substantive prose is retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains a GLM-4.6 block. Figure 1 shifts upward, Table 1 moves from page 6 to page 5, and surrounding text reflows. Figure artwork and appendix displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Relative to v2, the additional GLM-4.6 comparison provides limited evidence of applicability beyond GPT/Qwen, and the code link improves access information. These are modest gains: GLM offline-update results are absent, implementation/release documentation remains inconsistent, and removing the cognitive background reduces explanation and attribution. The original method and empirical evidence remain intact.
